See also: Aquarium and aquàrium

English

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *h₂ékʷeh₂
Proto-Italic *akʷā
Latin aqua
Proto-Indo-European *-yósder.
Proto-Italic *-āsios
Latin -ārius
Latin aquārius
Latin aquāriumbor.
English aquarium

    Borrowed from Latin aquārium, neuter of aquārius (“of or pertaining to water”), from aqua +‎ -arium. Doublet of ewer; see also Aquarius. Also claimed to be coined by English naturalist Philip Henry Gosse, as a blend of aquatic +‎ vivarium.[1]

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • (General American) enPR: ə-kwârʹē-əm, IPA(key): /əˈkwɛɹ.i.jəm/, /-ɛɹiəm/
    • Audio (US):(file)

    Noun

    [edit]

    aquarium (plural aquaria or aquariums)

    2. A tank, often made of glass, for keeping live fish or other aquatic animals.
      Synonym: (informal) fish tank
    4. A public place where live fish and other aquatic animals are exhibited.

    Usage notes

    [edit]

    The plural aquaria is generally considered more formal than aquariums.

    Derived terms

    [edit]
    • aquariumlike
    • boy aquarium
    • Macquarium
    • nonaquarium
    • seaquarium
    • submarium

    Dutch

    [edit]

    Etymology

    [edit]

    Borrowed from Latin aquārium. Influenced by English aquarium. Doublet of aker.

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • IPA(key): /aːˈkʋaː.ri.ʏm/
    • Audio:(file)
    • Hyphenation: aqua‧ri‧um
    • Rhymes: -aːriʏm

    Noun

    [edit]

    aquarium n (plural aquaria or aquariums, diminutive aquariumpje n)

    1. aquarium
    2. (obsolete) water basin, water tank

    Derived terms

    [edit]
    • zeeaquarium

    Related terms

    [edit]
    • aker

    French

    [edit]

    Etymology

    [edit]

    Borrowed from Latin aquārium. Doublet of évier.

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • IPA(key): /a.kwa.ʁjɔm/
    • Audio:(file)
    • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
    • Audio (France):(file)
    • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
    • Homophone: aquariums

    Noun

    [edit]

    aquarium m (plural aquariums)

    1. aquarium
    2. (slang) a clambake (an instance of smoking in an enclosed space)

    Further reading

    [edit]
    • “aquarium”, in Trésor de la langue française informatisé [Digitized Treasury of the French Language], 2012
